headline_marked: [[Argentina stages dramatic comeback]] to beat Egypt 3-2, reach World Cup quarterfinals
headline: Argentina stages dramatic comeback to beat Egypt 3-2, reach World Cup quarterfinals
summary: Inspired by Lionel Messi, Argentina scored three goals in the final 11 minutes to secure a stunning victory after trailing 2-0. Coach Lionel Scaloni was left speechless by the emotional rollercoaster.
details: Argentina's World Cup dreams were on the brink of collapse against Egypt, trailing 2-0 with just 11 minutes left in the match. The reigning champions faced a shocking exit from the tournament.

However, a late surge, ignited by captain Lionel Messi, turned the tide. Messi first assisted Cristian Romero's header in the 79th minute, then scored the equalizer himself four minutes later, electrifying the crowd.

The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Enzo Fernandez scored a stunning winner, securing a 3-2 victory and a spot in the quarterfinals. The team's resilience mirrored their previous extra-time thriller against Cape Verde.
Coach Lionel Scaloni was overcome with emotion, struggling to articulate his feelings after the match. "I'm really emotional right now," he admitted in a post-match interview.
Despite missing a penalty earlier in the game, Messi's decisive contributions proved crucial. Egypt also had a goal disallowed by VAR in the second half, adding to the match's drama.
Argentina will now face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarter-finals, with Scaloni expressing immense pride in his team's unwavering determination.
caption:
Down 2-0 with 11 minutes left, Argentina stages one of the most dramatic comebacks in World Cup history, powered by Lionel Messi!

See how they fought back to reach the quarterfinals.

Argentina's World Cup dreams were on the brink of collapse against Egypt, trailing 2-0 with just 11 minutes left in the match. The reigning champions faced a shocking exit from the tournament.

However, a late surge, ignited by captain Lionel Messi, turned the tide. Messi first assisted Cristian Romero's header in the 79th minute, then scored the equalizer himself four minutes later, electrifying the crowd.

The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Enzo Fernandez scored a stunning winner, securing a 3-2 victory and a spot in the quarterfinals. The team's resilience mirrored their previous extra-time thriller against Cape Verde.

Coach Lionel Scaloni was overcome with emotion, struggling to articulate his feelings after the match. "I'm really emotional right now," he admitted in a post-match interview.

Despite missing a penalty earlier in the game, Messi's decisive contributions proved crucial. Egypt also had a goal disallowed by VAR in the second half, adding to the match's drama.

Argentina will now face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarter-finals, with Scaloni expressing immense pride in his team's unwavering determination.

headline_marked: [[Examiners face jail for unfair marking]] in Bangladesh exams
headline: Examiners face jail for unfair marking in Bangladesh exams
summary: Bangladesh parliament passes bill to punish examiners with up to 2 years in jail for deliberate mark manipulation in public exams.
details: The bill, passed yesterday, aims to curb malpractice in public examinations, including cheating, question paper leaks, and fake certificates. Examiners who deliberately award excessively high or low marks in public examinations, such as the SSC and HSC exams, will face up to two years' imprisonment.
The law defines a public examination as any examination conducted, regulated or organised by a university or education board. Conviction requires confirmation by a third examiner.

The bill also introduces a legal definition of 'digital manipulation', covering unauthorised access to public examination databases as well as the hacking, alteration, modification, deletion or suppression of examination-related data. Anyone found guilty of digital manipulation may face up to five years' imprisonment.

The legislation includes provisions to protect whistleblowers who provide credible information about examination-related offences. Their identities will be protected, and they will be safeguarded from legal liability and retaliation.
